chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man performed tawaf around the Kaaba, then went out and performed sa‘i between al-Safa and al-Marwa. While he was going between them, he remembered that he had left part of his tawaf of the House incomplete.
He عليه السلام said: "He returns to the House and completes his tawaf, then returns to al-Safa and al-Marwa and completes what remains."

key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Safa, one of the two points of sa‘i
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Kaaba, the sacred structure around which tawaf is performed
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwa, the other point of sa‘i
key_terms.طَوَافِهِ: his tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the House

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if he remembers during sa‘i that his tawaf was incomplete?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning someone who begins the sa‘i between al-Safa and al-Marwa before fully completing tawaf. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that he must return to the Kaaba, complete the missing portion of tawaf, and then resume sa‘i from where he left off, showing the required order of these hajj and ʿumrah rites.
